Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife transferred nearly 60 million shares, worth over $10.5 billion, into an irrevocable family trust in March, according to SEC filings reviewed by Barron's.

The transfer followed a 10-year estate-planning strategy using trusts initially funded with approximately $51 million in Nvidia shares in 2016.

Estate attorneys say the structure could allow the accumulated gains to pass to heirs without federal estate tax.

The transfer preceded Huang's resignation and Nvidia's recent stock selloff.

text:
Bitcoin mining software firm Luxor hacked: attackers steal 0.243 $BTC in rewards from miners

"In case you're wondering, what Luxor does is they make software that lets Bitcoin miners manage their machines. So it's not doing the mining, it's the software that does the management."

"Attackers were able to compromise that software, apparently using AI, and changed where the machines sent their mining work. So the miners kept paying for the electricity and doing the actual mining, but the attacker collected the Bitcoin rewards, which were sent to their wallet."

"It wasn't a huge amount, but again, another novel attack surface that nobody had seen coming for crypto-related software, and it becomes absolutely exhausting."

"So far this is only 0.243 Bitcoin. But if you're mining Bitcoin or looking at Bitcoin miners or using software that's related to it, now you have to be worried about that as well."

"The miners got the electricity bill for it, but the hacker got the direct deposit."

Key takeaways from my latest industry survey and research conclusions:

1. Order visibility and shipment plans:
Strong new orders from OpenAI and Anthropic have extended Google TPU shipment visibility to 2029, ahead of Nvidia GPUs and other AI ASICs (mostly 4Q27–2Q28).

(1) From 2028, v9 will become the mainstay of Google’s own compute buildout, so v8-series orders (8t / 8i or their design variants) can be viewed as coming from OpenAI and Anthropic.

$OSCR "Owned" is doing heroic work in that sentence.

Joshua Kushner co-founded Oscar in 2012 and sits as Vice Chair. His Thrive funds hold about 14% of the economics. The other 86% is public float, with Vanguard and BlackRock the largest holders in it. What he kept is voting control, 68% of the vote through super-voting Class B shares at 20 votes a share, and even that sunsets in 2028.
